Buy a Danish Green Card on Telegram

A Danish green card sold on Telegram is either a replica, a registered original, or a genuine document with your details typed in. Those three are priced differently and fail differently, and the advert rarely says which.

Document type
A green card is the United States permanent resident card. Outside the United States the same job is done by a permanent residence card, and sellers use the American term loosely for every country.

buy danish green card on telegram – the short version

If you want the short version, a Danish green card bought through Telegram is only worth the money when three things line up. The stock has to match what SIRI uses, the number has to follow that office format, and the seller has to survive a question about a feature a photocopier cannot copy.

Work through the rest of this page with the card in front of you if you can. The numbered process later on is the sequence to follow and the checks list is what to look for at each step.

Buy a Green Card via Telegram: how the transaction works

Ask for the issue date and the issuing office before you ask the price. A seller working with SIRI stock answers instantly. A reseller has to go and look, and that pause tells you where you sit in the chain.

If the seller wants to move to another app for payment, that is normal, but keep the conversation on Telegram. The chat is the only record that survives a disappearing account.

Who actually issues a Green Card

In Denmark the office behind the green card is SIRI. The local name is permanent opholdstilladelse. Use the local name in the chat and the seller immediately knows whether you have done any reading.

Register access varies. Some countries let you check a number online, some need the holder, some need a call. Ask the seller what route exists and expect a specific answer rather than a general one.

Replica or registered original

Never accept the word original as a category. It is an adjective. The specification is the register, and a register either answers or it does not.

Whichever tier you buy, ask for it in writing. A one-line message saying the number does or does not resolve is worth more than any amount of reassurance in prose.

What a fair price looks like

Observed adverts for a Danish green card cluster between 2200–7200 DKK. That is the range to hold in your head, and it is deliberately wide because it covers three different products.

There is a floor below which the maths stops working for the seller. Below roughly the bottom third of the band, nobody is buying stock, so nobody is selling you stock.

The buying process, step by step

Run this sequence once, properly, rather than half of it three times with three sellers.

  1. Ask which office issued it and confirm the answer is SIRI.
  2. Request an uncropped photo of the full card on a plain surface with the laminate edge in frame.
  3. Request a UV shot of the data page and a close crop of the number field.
  4. Test the number against the format SIRI uses. A number that breaks the format ends the deal.
  5. Agree a price inside the 2200–7200 DKK band and pay in two parts, deposit then balance against tracking.
  6. On arrival check the document against the photos before you accept delivery and photograph the unopened envelope.

Checks that catch bad stock

Do these in daylight, with the card in your hand, and never accept a photo as proof of any of them.

  • Check the licence for the EU category grid and the Danish civil register reference.
  • Confirm the passport crown printing and the machine-readable zone.
  • Check the number format against the published rule for SIRI. Constructed numbers cannot be invented by hand.
  • Look for the UV print with a 365 nanometre torch. Real ink is sharp and placed deliberately. A print shows a dull bloom or nothing.
  • Loupe the microprint and the ghost image. Both collapse into a dotted line or a grey patch on a photocopy.
  • Compare the data across every field for internal consistency. A postcode that contradicts the state or the office area is a tell.
  • Check the laminate or polycarbonate edge for a fused seal rather than a cut line under a laid sheet.

Red flags that should end the conversation

If you see any of these, stop paying attention to the price.

  • A document where the final four digits of the civil register number are round numbers such as 0000.
  • The seller cannot name the issuing office, only the country.
  • The number breaks the published format, or is round and repeating.

Frequently asked questions

What does a green card cost on Telegram?

Between 350 and 1600 US dollars. The top of the band is where a number that resolves at the immigration office should sit.

Is a green card the same as a residence permit?

In the United States yes, in practice. Elsewhere the green card is the permanent tier and the residence permit is the fixed term tier below it.

Can the number be checked?

Only against the immigration register. Ask the seller which register the number sits in and expect a specific answer.

Why are green cards so expensive?

Because the number carries the most weight of any document here and the register check is the hardest to fake.

What is the usual fake?

A high quality print of a real card with the number left intact and the personal details changed.
